entries.heading: *Lee's Summit Tigers - Brian -
entries.narrative: He is back in 2019 and still lives in Missouri. As soon as he rejoined the league, this team has been active in trades and free agency. Since he has returned, he has won a Manager of the Year award and advanced to the Super Bowl in Season 16 only to fall to Cathedral. Brian finally moved past Creston in playoff wins and regular season wins in 2025. Brian has added OROY with QB CJ Stroud and 2 Defensive Player of the Year with LB Foyesade Oluokun and Zaire Franklin. He set a record for Closest win by 0.04. He is sitting at 10th overall in wins.

entries.heading: Great Falls Bison - Tim M -
entries.narrative: He came in and picked up the pieces in 2016 after Tony screwed this team over. I had played with Tim in a league long ago and knew that he would be a quality owner to help rebuild this team back to Playoff caliber. The 1st year was tough and finished 4-15 and won the Jamarcus Russell Trophy but year #2 was a winning year again even though not a Playoff year. The team is on its way back up. 2019 was a rough year for Tim. He had a lot of things going in his personal life and wasn't devoted as he would've like to have been. He finished the season 9-10 and on the outside of the Playoffs again. He finishes our league with a 23-34 record and no Playoffs.

entries.heading: Hinsdale Pacers -
entries.narrative: Ricky - He is a friend of Jake(Turkeyfoot) and has been co-owner with him for a while. Since Oak Ridge left he decided to take over the open team. He made it thru the draft and then that was it. Career record of 0-0. Maybe he should've stayed as co-owner with Jake. Ricky don't lose that number, it's the only one you own. You might use it if you feel better, when you get home.

entries.heading: ​ *Oak Ridge -
entries.narrative: Tony - He lives in Michigan and is the brother-in-law of Creston. Made for nice family feud. Left in 2015. He had never played fantasy football until joining the league but was a valuable member from the beginning. Tony played 10 seasons with us and made the Playoffs in 6 of the 1st 7 of them. Tony won his division once. He finished with an 8-4 Playoff record winning 2 SuperBowls and losing 1. He had a 99-91 overall record. He won several awards with 3 MVPs in 2009, 10 & 11(Aaron Rodgers twice and Arian Foster). He shares a record for Most consecutive Wins at 13. He holds the record for Most points in a Season by a player with 363.1. The disturbing thing about his departure was that he started trading off his team in bad trades before leaving. I didn't expect this from him. Jerk!
